name: cradle
_note: the lower hand holding the underside of the bump (still q_k4_down_0, after Harry's photo): the palm on its lower front, the fingers side by side along the curve, fanned a few degrees (s up to 6°) so their four ROUND tips step down round the underside, the little finger shortest; the thumb lying along the top of the hand with a narrow V to the index (ts 8; at 18 it stood off the hand), its end joints bent a little toward the bump (t 16/14; straight it read as 'a stiff bar'). v6's first 'cradle' curled ~75-90° ('a rake'); its second, fingers together with an even curl, ended in a column ('four even parallel stripes'); v7's steep grade ran the tips together into one point ('a flipper', 'a paddle'). Picked side by side with the still (tools/hand_shapes.py, lessons 51-52). v14: fanned less (s −3…3, was up to 6°): with the slimmer hand (palmW .27, fingerK .9, a long slim thumb) the tips meet at the bump's edge in one diagonal as the still's do; fanned 6° they stood out past it in a column, 'a stub thumb, tips stacked' (natural lens v13; lesson 56)
